findings.evidence: `instFiberBundle`: `trivializationAtlas' := range (fun p : Frame (F := F) D × Basis Unit ℂ F ↦ p.1.trivialization A p.2)`. `exists_frame` uses `A.modelEquiv` only through `A.modelEquiv.finrank_eq.trans (finrank_self ℂ)`. `compare`'s docstring: 'comparison between the holomorphic structures built from two choices of model coordinate for the same operator'.
findings.fix: Replace the field with `finrank : finrank ℂ F = 1`, so every field is a Prop and two packagings of the same `D` give definitionally equal fibres and instances. Choose the basis for `trivializationAt'` classically, e.g. `Basis.singleton`-based or `(finBasisOfFinrankEq ℂ F finrank).reindex`. Then drop the whole `compare*` block, and let `toHolomorphicLineOperator` simply store `hF`.
findings.issue: The field `modelEquiv : F ≃L[ℂ] ℂ` is data that never affects the construction. `trivializationAtlas'` ranges over all `Frame × Basis Unit ℂ F`; the coordinate is used only to pick `trivializationAt'` (via `modelBasis`) and to re-derive `finrank ℂ F = 1` in `exists_frame`. Because of it, `Fiber` and the bundle instances depend on a non-canonical choice, and `compare`, `compare_mk`, `compare_self`, `compare_symm`, `toOriginalHomeomorph_compare`, `compare_trans` and the private `contMDiff_compare` exist only to identify bundles built from different choices.

summary: `HolomorphicLineOperator` stores the choice `modelEquiv : F ≃L[ℂ] ℂ` even though the atlas already uses every frame and every model basis, so the holomorphic structure never depends on it. The comparison API in `HolomorphicBundle.lean` (`compare` through `compare_trans`, plus `contMDiff_compare`) only handles this unused choice; the Prop `finrank ℂ F = 1` would be enough.
